introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 3 (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: three and a quarter hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR QUESTIONS in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing ONE question from SECTION B and TWO questions from Section C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each. Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references. Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed. Materials required: Topographic map, Graph Paper and two outline maps of Cameroon.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B: FIELDWORK AND TECHNIQUES**

2. Based on fieldwork you have undertaken either in Physical or Human Geography, choose **one** of the following topics:

- (a) Channel characteristics
- (b) Down slope variation in size and depth of gullies
- (c) Vegetation characteristics
- (d) A modern factory or cottage industry
- (e) Land use in a rural or an urban area
- (f) Shopping patterns in a shopping centre
incertitudes: Règle de choix : le sujet impose « Answer FOUR questions in all : question ONE (obligatoire, 31 marks), ONE question de la Section B et TWO de la Section C ». `regles_choix` porte le minimum exprimable par section (B : 1 sur 2 ; C : 2 sur 4) ; la question 1 (Section A) est obligatoire donc sans règle ; la consigne complète (4 questions en tout) est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.

Points : Q1 = 31 (7+4+7+6+3+4), Q2 à Q7 = 23 chacune (Q2 : 5+3+2+3+8+2 ; Q3 : 12+2+3+4+2 ; Q4 : 6+6+6+5 ; Q5 : 4+10+9 ; Q6 : 6+12+5 ; Q7 : 5+10+8), soit 100 points pour les 4 questions à traiter ; aucun écart avec les totaux imprimés en page de garde. Pour les blocs à plusieurs items (Q1 a, c, d), `points` de la sous-question est la somme des points imprimés des items.

Sujet scanné de 5 pages (page de garde, questions 1 à 7, carte topographique de Kumba avec sa légende, fond de carte du Cameroun) ; filigranes et bandeaux gcerevision.com ignorés. Contrairement à d'ordinaires Paper 3, la carte de Kumba et le fond de carte du Cameroun SONT dans le PDF et ont été recadrés en PNG (la carte, pivotée de 90 degrés sur la page, a été remise à l'endroit). Le papier millimétré n'est pas fourni.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au niveau Advanced Level. Aucune statistique précise n'est avancée sauf celles du tableau imprimé de la Q3 ; les ordres de grandeur géographiques (pluviométries, altitudes, dates de création d'organismes) sont donnés de façon prudente et sont à faire relire par un géographe avant mise en avant.

Q2 : question de travail de terrain à réponse personnelle : le sujet demande au candidat de répondre d'après SON propre terrain. Le corrigé est un modèle générique (suivi complet pour le thème (a), équivalents donnés pour (b) à (f)) ; aucune donnée réelle n'est avancée, les valeurs numériques (largeur 3,0 m, profondeur 0,4 m, vitesse 0,5 m/s) sont purement illustratives et signalées comme telles.
Q2 : les sous-questions (i) à (vi) sont les parties imprimées de la question ; les thèmes (a) à (f) de l'énoncé sont recopiés dans l'introduction de l'exercice.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i) Locate the area where the field work was carried out. *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*Model answer: the candidate must answer from his or her own fieldwork. The model below follows the whole enquiry for topic (a), Channel characteristics, and gives the equivalent points for the other five topics. Any numerical values quoted are illustrative only, not data from a real survey.*

**What to write.** Name the exact place, then fix it step by step from the large scale to the small scale, and add a sketch map.
1. *Administrative location:* region, division and the nearest town, with the distance and direction from it (for example "a stream about 4 km north-east of the school, in X Division").
2. *Geographical location:* approximate latitude and longitude, or a grid reference on the topographic map, and the position relative to a main road, river or relief feature.
3. *Physical/human setting:* altitude, relief, climate, vegetation or land use, which show why the site was suitable.
4. *Sketch map:* a clearly annotated location map with the main roads, the stream or site, a north arrow, a scale, a key and a title; a small map of Cameroon with the region shaded helps.

**Marking guide.** Administrative position 1, relative position/distance 1, coordinates or grid reference 1, annotated sketch map 2. A vague statement ("near my town") earns at most 1 mark.

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii) State your objective and hypothesis. *(3 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Objective.** A clear aim stated with an infinitive verb. Topic (a): *To investigate how the characteristics of a stream channel (width, depth, velocity and discharge) change downstream.*

**Hypothesis.** A testable statement that can be accepted or rejected. Topic (a): *Channel width, depth, velocity and discharge increase downstream.*

**Equivalent for the other topics (examples).**
- (b) Gullies: *to find out how the size and depth of gullies vary down the slope; gully width and depth increase down the slope.*
- (c) Vegetation: *to study vegetation characteristics along a transect; plant height, cover and number of species change with distance from the road (or with altitude).*
- (d) Factory or cottage industry: *to find out why the industry is located where it is; the industry is located here because of raw materials, labour and the market.*
- (e) Land use: *to identify land uses; land use changes with distance from the centre (urban) or from the village (rural).*
- (f) Shopping: *to find out why people use the centre; people travel farther for comparison goods than for convenience goods.*

**Marking guide.** Objective 1, hypothesis 1, relevance and clarity of both 1.

questions.enonce_markdown: (iii) Which materials did you use to carry out your investigation? *(2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
List the instruments **and** the stationery, and say what each is used for. Topic (a): a measuring tape (about 30 m), ranging poles, a metre rule or graduated stick, a float (an orange or cork), a stop-watch, a thermometer, a field notebook, pencils, a clipboard, a camera and recording sheets.

**For the other topics.** (b) tape, ruler, clinometer (slope), ranging poles, recording sheets; (c) quadrats, tape, identification guide, notebook, camera; (d) questionnaire/interview schedule, notebook, camera, base map; (e) base map, colour pencils, notebook, tally sheets; (f) questionnaires, tally sheets, base map, clipboard.

**Marking guide.** 2 marks for at least four relevant items correctly identified; a single item or an unrelated list earns 1 mark at most.

questions.enonce_markdown: (iv) How did the materials assist you in your findings? *(3 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Link each material to the measurement it made possible.
- The *tape measure* gave the channel width and the distances between the sampling stations.
- The *metre rule* gave depth at regular points across the channel, so that the mean depth and the cross-sectional area (width $\times$ mean depth) could be calculated.
- The *float and stop-watch* gave the velocity of the surface water: velocity = distance / time.
- The *ranging poles* fixed the straight line of the cross-section and the stations.
- The *notebook and recording sheets* kept the data in an orderly form, and the *camera* gave photographs of the sites as evidence for the report.
- Together they gave accurate, comparable data at each station, which allowed the hypothesis to be tested.

**Other topics.** A clinometer gives the slope angle (b); a quadrat gives a fixed sampling area and so a fair comparison of plant cover (c); a questionnaire provides first-hand opinions and reasons (d, f).

**Marking guide.** 1 mark for each material linked to its use, up to 3.

questions.enonce_markdown: (v) How was your data processed and presented? *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Processing (4 marks).** Raw data are cleaned, organised in a table and converted into useful values.
- *Averages:* mean width, mean depth and mean velocity for each station (add the values and divide by the number of readings).
- *Cross-sectional area* $A = \text{width} \times \text{mean depth}$ ($\text{m}^2$).
- *Discharge* $Q = A \times v$ ($\text{m}^3\,\text{s}^{-1}$). Illustrative example only: width 3.0 m, mean depth 0.4 m, velocity 0.5 m s$^{-1}$ gives $A = 1.2\ \text{m}^2$ and $Q = 1.2 \times 0.5 = 0.6\ \text{m}^3\,\text{s}^{-1}$.
- *Velocity* $v = d/t$ (distance of float travel divided by time, repeated three times and averaged).
- *Percentages, ranks or a statistical test*: for example Spearman's rank correlation coefficient $r_s = 1 - \dfrac{6\sum d^2}{n(n^2-1)}$ to test the relationship between distance downstream and channel size (for other topics: percentage of land-use types, mean gully depth, species counts or percentage of respondents).

**Presentation (4 marks).**
- *Tables* of the raw and processed data for every station.
- *Graphs:* a line graph of width, depth and velocity against distance downstream (or a long profile), or bar graphs for comparison.
- *Cross-section diagrams* of the channel at each station, drawn to scale on graph paper.
- *Scatter graph* with a best-fit line for the relationship tested.
- *Maps and photographs:* annotated field sketches and located photographs; for human geography, land-use maps (choropleth or proportional circles), pie charts of percentages and flow lines.
- *Description and interpretation* of each graph in a few sentences.

**Marking guide.** Processing methods with formulae 4; presentation techniques named and described 4. Both must be linked to the topic chosen.

State whether the hypothesis is **accepted** or **rejected**, and support the statement with the main evidence from the findings. Topic (a), model: *The results confirmed the hypothesis: channel width, depth, velocity and discharge increased from the upstream to the downstream station, because the volume of water increases as tributaries and run-off join the river and the channel becomes larger and more efficient.* Add one or two sentences on limits of the study (a small number of stations, one season, the rough float method) and, if possible, a suggestion for improvement.

**Marking guide.** Clear acceptance or rejection with the main evidence 1 mark; a brief explanation or limitation 1 mark.
